headlines.article_text: USPS plans 11% package fuel surcharge but no first-class stamp hike Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu A United States Postal Service (USPS) worker carries containers and packages from a vehicle in Tracy, California, US, on Wednesday, March 25, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images The cash-strapped United States Postal Service said on Thursday it is seeking ​approval for an 11% price hike for domestic priority mail and ‌package deliveries in January to deal with rising fuel costs. USPS, which needs approval from the Postal Regulatory Commission for the price increase, said it was not planning to hike the price of first-class stamps in January, which rose in July from 78 to 82 cents. The surcharge is rising from a temporary 8% surcharge that was imposed in April. USPS said this week its transportation expenses in the 12 months ending September 30 rose by $225 million due to higher fuel costs. USPS said it was proposing to hike overall domestic shipping services prices 5.9% on average and is raising prices by an average of 7.9% for international deliveries. USPS asked Congress on Tuesday for $2 billion in support and reimbursements as its head warned ​the agency would be forced to make significant cuts in retail post ‌offices and other reductions unless lawmakers act. USPS reported an annual $6.5 billion loss versus a net loss of $9 billion in the prior 12 months. The ​new Democratic-led Congress, which takes office in January, will need to decide whether ​to help the Postal Service after Republicans held a series of hearings ⁠over the last two years on its finances. USPS wants $2 billion from Congress for ​unfunded requirements it has imposed. The agency has recorded net losses of more than $120 billion since ​2007. The volume of first-class mail, its most profitable product, fell this year to its lowest level since 1965 as consumers have moved to digital communication, while USPS must still pay for costly ​nationwide delivery. Postmaster General David Steiner says the ⁠agency has a broken business model and needs help from lawmakers to turn around its operations. In May, ⁠USPS ​suspended non-essential spending on travel, office supplies and consultants. ​USPS also earlier this year temporarily suspended employer payments for a federal pension program. headlines.article_text: Nebius Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Nebius results surpassed consensus, but full-year guidance was light. The report comes after fellow neoclouds IREN and CoreWeave showed better-than-expected results in the past week. The companies' stocks have bounced back this week after a brutal past month that reflected concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout. Nvidia, which invests across the neocloud space, is creating added volatility due to the crisis surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. In this article NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Arkady Volozh, CEO of Nebius and then Yandex CEO, speaks at the Artificial Intelligence Journey event in Moscow on Nov. 9, 2019. Mikhail Svetlov | Getty Images Nebius shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds issued disappointing full-year revenue guidance. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: 31 cents adjusted vs. loss of 69 cents per share expected Revenue: $980.8 million vs. $907.5 million expected Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement . The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier. The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to $3.4 billion range. Analysts surveyed by LSEG had $3.37 billion. Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our buildout." The LSEG consensus was $11.98 billion. The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion. Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion. Nebius stock chart. Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%. Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report. Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027. During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing. "Capital markets have been unsettled lately," CEO Arkady Volozh said on a conference call with analysts. "Two questions are being asked our whole industry, how fast can AI build-out happen, and who will pay for it? These are important questions. The way I think about it is simple. The demand for AI is real and substantial. Everything else, like building the capacity and financing it, is just a task. Tasks can be hard, but they all can be solved." The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress. headlines.summary: Cosm has secured a new studio partnership with Disney that will bring "Star Wars: A New Hope" to its domes as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration.
headlines.article_text: 'Star Wars' is coming to Cosm domes ahead of 50th anniversary Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Cosm has partnered with Disney on a multiyear, multifilm deal that will kick off with "Star Wars: A New Hope" early next year. This is Cosm's third studio deal — it already has partnerships with Universal and Warner Bros. — and sixth theatrical release. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for a unique presentation of the film. In this article DIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A poster for Disney and Lucasfilm's "Star Wars: A New Hope" in shared reality at Cosm. Cosm The Force is strong with Cosm. On Thursday, the immersive entertainment technology company announced a new studio partnership with The Walt Disney Co. that will bring the original "Star Wars" to its domes early next year as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Cosm's massive concave screens will drop film fans into a galaxy far, far away starting in March, just ahead of the Academy Award-winning film's 50th anniversary in May. "We are thrilled to add the Disney partnership," Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. "We do look for those opportunities of these like anniversary and commemorative moments. We look for those opportunities to celebrate with the fans, but also find this mutually beneficial partnership between both parties." This will be Cosm's sixth theatrical collaboration with Hollywood, having already partnered with Warner Bros. to bring "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. The company is set to launch immersive screenings of Universal's "Shrek" in December. Each Cosm dome has stadium-style seating, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width fills much of the viewers' periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the onscreen environment. Cosm's LA venue playing "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" in shared reality. Courtesy of Cosm In this case, "Star Wars" will be displayed in a large rectangle in the center of the dome while the background is transformed into the iconic planets of Tatooine and Yavin IV that are featured in the film as well as the infamous Death Star. Audiences will also see elements that will make it appear like they're traveling at lightspeed and getting trapped in an intergalactic trash compactor. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for the unique presentation of the film. "We look for those moments where sound, music ... listening to Darth Vader's breath for the first time ... you feel those moments differently in an 87-foot diameter dome and 12k resolution with the sound system we have," Scalice said. "And it's one of the things that with experiential cinema and our technology that we were so excited and honestly privileged that we can take these defining moments for fans and work closely with our partners that doesn't really change the authenticity of it, it just enhances it in a different manner." The premium experience will also be paired with a themed menu. Cosm has done this with other titles, such as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," serving guests throughout the screening with house-made shepherd's pie, pretzel wands with cheese dip and a box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans. Cosm is trying to establish itself as a destination for fandom — both for sports and for film. It has a wide variety of live event offerings, which it telecasts using proprietary cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, as well as its expanding library of movies. "What I love is that we really are kind of building these Cosm communities built on fandom," Scalice said. "It's the No. 1 foundation for our business." And Star Wars is a powerful fandom. The franchise remains one of the top-ranking pieces of intellectual property across film, television and retail annually, and Disney is gearing up for a massive celebration of its semicentennial including merchandise launches, theatrical re-releases, its biannual Star Wars Celebration convention and collaborations with other brands.
